notes: Checks run from the repo root. A check that runs its work in a container or on another host (docker exec, kubectl exec, ssh) needs a 'cleanup' command: a check killed at the gate cap takes only its local client with it, so the gate runs 'cleanup' after a timeout, with the same $MYSPEC_CHECK_RUN_ID the check saw. Have the check record its remote PID in a file named after $MYSPEC_CHECK_RUN_ID, and have 'cleanup' kill that PID's process group. Containers (a top-level 'containers' map and a check's 'runIn'): see "Per-check settings" in docs/stop-gate.md of the myspec plugin. Give a check a non-empty 'diffCommand' when its plain 'command' already fails on the default branch: the gate runs 'diffCommand' instead, with $MYSPEC_BASE_REF exported as the merge base with the default branch. Scope the command to that range and guard it against an empty file set, e.g. files=$(git diff --name-only --diff-filter=ACMR $MYSPEC_BASE_REF -- '*.ts'); [ -z "$files" ] || npx eslint $files. Give a check "paths", a list of repo-relative globs, to run it only when a file this session wrote in the checkout matches one: '*' and '?' stay within one path segment, '**' as a whole segment spans any number of them, a trailing '/' means everything under it, and each glob matches the whole path from the repo root ('**/*.py' for any depth). A path git reports changed in the checkout (uncommitted, untracked, or against the base) also runs the check when it matches, because the session record misses rm, git revert and generated files. A required check skipped this way is named in the stop message. Without paths a check always runs, and so does every check when the session's writes are unknown.
